defect: eval_golden._first_complete_json (the gguf backend's parse) required the legacy wire key "action", while seeds/prompt_template.txt, eval/golden_corpus.jsonl, the CNR training corpus and the app's LlamaCommandInterpreter grammar all use the canonical "intent" key. Every correct model completion was discarded as NO-JSON and scored as an abstention (predict_gguf returned {"action": "none"}), so a live gguf run could not measure any working model.
why_now: exposed by the first real gguf run on this branch (T-183 phase B): the stdgate-qwen-s43-chat-v17 run logged NO-JSON on valid intent-shaped JSON; the live probe reproduced it deterministically (raw output {"intent": "call", ...} -> parsed {"action": "none", "confidence": 0.0}). results.csv has zero recorded gguf rows, so the path had never been exercised in this repo.
repro: v17-dial: .venv/bin/python -c "import eval_golden; eval_golden.predict_gguf('माइयालाई फोन गर', cfg, gguf)" -> [gguf] NO-JSON output for ...: '{"intent": "call", ...}' -> {'action': 'none', 'confidence': 0.0}
fix: minimal canonical-key bridge inside _first_complete_json only (its single caller is predict_gguf): accept a complete object carrying the canonical string "intent" and normalize it onto the metric layer's historic "action" name (value passed through untouched); legacy action-shaped completions are accepted exactly as before and win when both keys are present. No metric, threshold, fixture or corpus was touched.
